title: I've spent 19 years on my dream sci-fi game. People call it "AI slop" and a "scam" without reading a single line or playing a single minute. And yes I used Fable 5.2 and Opus 5.5 for some parts of the game.
author: Emergency-Reply-5437
selftext:
I need to get something off my chest.

I've been working on this game since 2007 – 19 years now – back when I was a teenager in school. It's inspired by StarFox (which always felt too short), but with the humor, fast action, exploration, and wildly varied enemies I always missed in other sci-fi games. A story packed with humor at the center. That's what I set out to build.

A few months from now, it'll be finished. 15 to 30 hours of gameplay depending on how you play. Over 20 worlds to explore. A gripping story based on my novel trilogy – over 3,000 pages, with the first book professionally lektorized at around 450 pages. This is my life's work.

Demo should be ready soon for Steam. Since I head a lot about people cloning indie projects I am not sure to host a demo since it's just my life's work and I don't want some random AI Gaming Company's just to copy my game before it is finished. And after so many years I aim to release it in February 2027. 

And here's the part that's been eating at me.

I've gotten a lot of hate lately. People insult me, call it "AI slop," call it a scam game. The thing is – many of them haven't read a single word about it. Haven't watched the trailer. Haven't played a single minute. Meanwhile, my best friends have played it. They've seen it. They know what it is.

The ideas go back to a time before AI even existed. The first graphics and drawings? No AI. Many of those haters weren't even born yet.

Yes, I use AI. I use many different AIs – so many I sometimes lose count. But I also work with local artists, local musicians, and real voice actors. I record my own voice lines with a Samson C3U studio mic. I believe development can go hand in hand. One doesn't exclude the other. The human component will always matter.

But I think it's dumb when people today refuse to use AI to speed up workflows. 90% of humanity seems to think you press a button and the AI spits out a finished game. That's not how it works. Even with AI, you still need 12–16 hours a day, brainpower, love, and a vision. I've sacrificed nearly two decades of my life for this.

I was recently at a university – 90% of games there are vibe-coded right now. The basics are still taught. The internet was never going to catch on either, right? Who needs smartphones? I always imagine those South Park rednecks who are against anything new.

For context: I'm not new to this. I was known as Sauron in the early German gaming scene of the 90s and 2000s. I worked on games like Vampires Dawn and Alone Eternal Nightmare, which received Players Choose Gold. I have my own wiki page. I know what I can do and what I can't.

So here's my question to you:

Does the trailer work for you? I had it made with Claude Opus 5.5 on the "very high" setting. It captures moments from the still-unfinished game.

I'm open to criticism. But please – actually watch it, read about it, or ask me something before you call it slop or a scam. My friends have played it. Strangers haven't. That's the difference.
